summary: The root عَفَّ (ʿaffa) primarily means to be chaste, modest, or to abstain from what is unlawful or unseemly.

provenance.lane: Edward William Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon (1863-93), public domain. Digital text via Perseus, Tufts University, CC BY-SA 3.0 US.
provenance.summary: Editorial summary derived from the Lane entry. NOT Lane's own wording. Shown as a gloss only; the Lane text below is the source.

headwords.def: عَفَّ, (S, O, Msb, K, &c.,) aor. عَفِفَ, (S, O, Msb,) inf. n. عِفَّةٌ and عَفَافٌ (S, O, Msb, K) and عَفٌّ and عَفَافَةٌ, (S, O, K,) He abstained (S, O, Msb, K) from ( عن ) what was unlawful, (S, O,) or from what was not lawful nor comely or decorous, (M, K,) or from things that should be sacred or inviolable, and base, or carnal, objects of inordinate desire, (TA,) or from a thing: (Msb:) [but it is implied in the K that the verb is used without the expression of the object, or objects; and it…
عَفَّفْتُهُ, inf. n. تَعْفِيفٌ, I gave him to drink what is termed عُفَافَة [q. v.]. (IDrd, O, K.)

اعفّهُ ٱللّٰهُ God made him to be عَفِيف [i. e. abstinent, &c.]. (S, O, Msb, K.) أَعَفَّتْ, [in the CK, erroneously, اُعِفَّت,] said of a ewe, or she-goat, is from العُفَافَةُ [and therefore signifies She had milk collected in her udder: or she had some milk remaining in her udder after most of it had been sucked ]. (IDrd, O, K.)
تعفّف: see 1. Also He (a man, S, O) drank what is termed عُفَافَة [q. v.]. (S, O, K.)

تَعَافَّ نَاقَتَكَ Milk thou thy camel after the first milking. (S, O, L, K.) And تعافّ said to a sick man, Treat thyself medically. (K.) One says, بِأَىِّ شَىْءٍ نَتَعَافُّ With what thing shall we treat ourselves medically ? (AA, O, TA.)
إِعْتَفَفَ see 1. اعتفّت الإِبِلُ اليَبِيسَ The camels took with the tongue [or licked up ] the dry herbage above the earth or dust, taking the best, or choice, thereof; as also. (O, K.)
إِسْتَعْفَفَ see 1, in two places: and see also 8.
عَفٌّ; and its fem.: see عَفيِفٌ.

عُفَّةٌ: see عُفَافَةٌ. Also An old woman: (Ibn-El-Faraj, O, K, TA:) like عُثَّةٌ: being formed [from the latter] by substitution. (TA.) And A certain fish, smooth, white, and small; when cooked, having a taste like that of rice. (Ibn-ElFaraj, O, K.)
عِفَافٌ A medicine, or remedy. (AA, O, K.)

عَفِيفٌ and epithets from عَفَّ, as such signifying Abstaining (S, O, Msb, K) from what is unlawful, (S, O,) or from what is not lawful nor comely or decorous, (K,) or from things that should be sacred or inviolable, and base, or carnal, objects of inordinate desire, (TA,) or from a thing: (Msb:) [and very often used as meaning abstinent, continent, chaste, virtuous, modest, decent, or decorous: ] fem.

عُفَافَةٌ is the subst. from عَفَّ said of milk: (O, K:) so says IDrd: (O:) [accord. to him, it app. signifies Milk that has collected in the udder: ] and it signifies (S, O, K) accord. to another or others, (O,) as also, somewhat of milk remaining in the udder (S, O, K) after most of it has been sucked.
جَآءَ عَلَى عِفَّانِ ٰلِكَ He (a man, S, O) came at the time of that: (S, O, K: *) a dial. var. of إِفَّان: (S, O:) or, accord. to IF, formed [from the latter] by substitution. (O.)

headword_note: Lane indexes geminate roots with two letters where the Corpus uses three; both spellings are resolved here.
